question: Should OpenClaw accept a core ACP node-backed runtime that expands the gateway-to-node command/event boundary, and what storage/security proof is required before this branch can proceed?
rationale: The feature is strategically plausible, but it changes durable runtime state, message delivery recovery, and node execution trust boundaries in ways automation should not approve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Hold for storage/security-ready runtime
options.body: Require SQLite-backed state, fixed source-level delivery/reconnect blockers, and redacted real paired-node proof before this PR can be considered for merge.

options.title: Sponsor as experimental core runtime
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the core direction and define a narrower default-off or staged merge path with named security and upgrade follow-up gates.

options.title: Close and replace with smaller slices
options.body: If this branch is too large to safely review, close it after opening or sponsoring smaller ACP node-runtime PRs that preserve the useful architecture work.

recommendation.title: Hold for storage/security-ready runtime
recommendation.body: Require SQLite-backed state, fixed source-level delivery/reconnect blockers, and redacted real paired-node proof before this PR can be considered for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on gateway/node command policy and security boundary acceptance, where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
